subject: POC/Trial planning: success criteria & RACI - Summit Health

Subject: POC/Trial planning: success criteria & RACI - Summit Health

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery so we have a shared starting point for the POC/trial. Please confirm or correct anything I’ve missed.

Scope we discussed:
- 2-week trial of Redwood inference for clinical note summarization on a 10k record sample (de-identified).
- Integration via API to your app (staging environment) with streaming responses and structured output.

Draft success criteria (attached spreadsheet):
1) Latency: median <= 250ms per request at expected concurrency (10-20 rps).
2) Accuracy: 85% semantic alignment vs. Summit internal labeling on the 500-record test set (per evaluation rubric in sheet).
3) Reliability: zero data exfil incidents, full audit logging enabled.
4) Ops: basic end-to-end integration + runbook for test runs.

Timeline (proposal):
- Confirm scope & RACI by 11/20
- Network/security checklist & access provided by Summit by 11/25
- Redwood infra readiness + model provisioning by 11/28
- Trial starts week of 11/29, 2 weeks duration

As discussed, can you confirm the owners for these areas so we can map a RACI? I’ve put an initial suggestion in the attached sheet (SummitHealth_MVP_success_criteria.xlsx). High-level roles we need: App owner (integration), Infra/Network owner (VPC, firewall), Security/GRC reviewer, Procurement contact for trial agreement/PO, and Business success owner.

Next steps (please):
- Emily: confirm owners + any timeline conflicts by 11/20
- I’ll schedule a short kick-off call the week of 11/29 once we have access and approvals

Attachments: SummitHealth_MVP_success_criteria.xlsx (success criteria + RACI draft)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few quick notes from the CSM/evangelism side:

- Evaluation plan: recommend an internal checkpoint after week 1 (demo + red flags) to validate the accuracy metric and tweak prompts. I added a "Week 1 checkpoint" row in the attached doc.
- Data ingestion: if Summit can provide a small 500-record seed set earlier (even synthetic/de-identified), we can pre-run model baseline metrics before the official start.
- Stakeholder mapping: we’ll need an internal business owner at Summit to sign off on the success criteria; Marissa called out the right roles.

Aditya — can you review the network/access assumptions in the sheet and flag any blockers? Neha, please call out any security artifacts we should request upfront (SOC 2 evidence, encryption in transit, audit log format).

Happy to sync on a 30-min tech kickoff next week.

Hi team — quick infra note and owners proposal.

Assumptions for the 2-week trial:
- Summit will provide a staging API endpoint (or VPC peering) with an allowlist for Redwood egress IPs. If VPC peering is preferred, we need a contact who owns cloud networking to coordinate.
- Dataset will be de-identified. We won’t persist PII. All request/response logs will be stored in Redwood audit logs; we can provide export.

Proposed ownership (RACI style) for trial operations: 
- App Integration: Responsible = Summit App Team (Tom Alvarez) / Accountable = Summit App Lead
- Network/Infra (VPC, firewall rules): Responsible = Summit Cloud Infra Team / Consulted = Aditya Rao (Redwood)
- Model Runtime & Serving: Responsible = Redwood Inference Ops (Aditya) / Accountable = Redwood Eng
- Security Review & Compliance: Responsible = Summit Security (Sonia Patel) / Consulted = Neha Kapoor (Redwood Security)
- Procurement / Trial Agreement: Responsible = Summit Procurement (Tom Alvarez) / Accountable = Summit Legal
- Business Success / Acceptance: Responsible = Summit Clinical Analytics Lead / Accountable = Emily Carter

Attachments: redwood-poc-network-checklist.pdf (network items we need to validate before start)

Open items for Summit to confirm by 11/20:
1) Who is the cloud/network owner we should loop in for VPC/allowlist?
2) Procurement contact for trial agreement and whether a PO is required before kickoff.

If Summit prefers we run the trial entirely in Redwood-managed infra (no peering), we can scope that option and provide a cost estimate — that will require a dedicated instance but speeds setup.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Infrastructure Lead (Redwood Inference)
